source_note: Brahme, Mehta, Matthews & Franks, 'Who blocks whom? Probabilistic pass-blocking assignments for evaluating blockers and pass rushers in American football', arXiv:2609.33664v2 [stat.AP], 29 Sep 2026 (Abhijit Brahme, Ishan Mehta, Gregory J. Matthews, Alexander Franks; UCSB / Loyola University Chicago), 30 pages; code on GitHub. Adapts Franks et al. 2015 basketball defensive-matchup HMM to football pass protection: frame-by-frame probabilistic blocker->rusher assignments in continuous time. Latent state = rusher identity; emission position bivariate normal on rusher-QB segment (mu=gamma_r R+gamma_q Q, core assumption blocker between rusher and QB) + von Mises orientation (face opposite rusher, kappa=1); transition stickiness rho with per-blocker Beta empirical-Bayes partial pooling; pre-snap multinomial-logistic prior (alignment/down/distance/formation); disengaged state with asymmetric shed (p_fail)/re-engage (rho_null). Eq1 STRAIN=-v/d (Nguyen 2023, central-difference 2nd-order). Metrics: front-normalized attention n_eff=sum theta; blocker assignment entropy; geometric+STRAIN beaten/won/release; Kaplan-Meier RMST + beat/shed rate (right-censored at throw); opponent-adjusted discrete-time logistic survival frailty (Trent Williams 15th->3rd); continuous-time assignment-weighted plus-minus on Delta STRAIN (filtered posterior no lookahead, AR(1) phi-hat=-0.059, attribute-archetype shrinkage z=[position,height,weight]); Eq4 pocket control PC=logit^-1(sum I_b - sum I_j) (Fernandez-Bornn 2018); Eq5 value-weighted near-QB space Q_k (V=exp(-dist/3yd), 5yd disk); directed assignment-flow space generation SGG (interior double-team generators). Data: 2023 NFL Big Data Bowl / Next Gen Stats 10Hz, 698 rushers/534 blockers/8530 plays, first 8 weeks 2021, PFF roles, snap->QB window, Kalman smoothing. Validation vs independent PFF charting: 44037 blocker-plays mean 0.77 engaged mass on charted rusher, 87.5% most-assigned agreement; rusher effect vs PFF pressure 0.57/sack 0.46 (strong), blocker effect vs pressures allowed 0.32 (directional). Params align football intuition (OL/TE gamma_r 0.82-0.89/rho 0.96-0.98; RB gamma_q 0.45/rho 0.39/p_fail 0.58). Limitations: positioning only (velocity complementary), cannot separate actively-impeding vs merely-in-right-place (missed block while assigned; two-layer HMM future), blocker evaluation associational not causal, STRAIN outcome-agnostic (any frame-level pressure measure substitutable). Extracted faithfully (not a derivative summary). Equations 1-5, transition, von Mises, logistic survival, attention, continuous APM, attribute model, space-generation weight printed in math font that extracts garbled; reconstructed in labeled LaTeX and flagged here and in assumptions. Domain football matches catalog (NFL offensive-line / pass-rush tracking analytics). Directly isomorphic to GSE's OL causal-breakdown assignment kernel, STRAIN pressure measure, partial-credit continuous plus-minus, opponent-adjusted block-sustain survival, pocket space-control surface, and teammate-freeing space-generation credit. No sportsbook lines/spreads/totals/implied odds in source or lifted into GSE.

primitives.name: Orientation modeled von Mises(eta_rusher+pi, kappa=1): blocker faces opposite rusher
primitives.verbatim_quote: Because orientation is a circular (angular) quantity, we model it directly with a von Mises distribution, the circular analogue of the Gaussian distribution

symbol_and_unit_ledger.I0: modified Bessel function of first kind, order zero

assumptions: Because orientation is a circular angular quantity, it is modeled directly with a von Mises distribution, the circular analogue of the Gaussian; given that they are guarding rusher j, blocker b's orientation is vonMises(eta_tj+pi, kappa) with density exp{-kappa cos(eta_tb-eta_tj)}/(2 pi I0(kappa)), where I0 is the modified Bessel function of the first kind of order zero and the mean direction eta_tj+pi encodes the blocker facing opposite the rusher; kappa=1 is fixed. The von Mises density is printed math-font and reconstructed here.

primitives.name: Pass blockers face the rusher and stay square during pass blocking

primitives.name: Transition: P(stay)=rho, P(switch)=(1-rho)/(n-1); encodes pass-off/stunt stickiness
primitives.verbatim_quote: which results in a switch in assignment during the course of the play

symbol_and_unit_ledger.rho^(g): per-position stickiness (probability of staying on engaged rusher)
symbol_and_unit_ledger.n_i: number of pass rushers on play i

assumptions: Offensive linemen may pass off rushers to teammates or stunt (feint toward a rusher then recover to the original assignment), which results in a switch in assignment during the course of the play; the model encodes this frame-to-frame stickiness with P(I_tbj=1|I_(t-1)bj=1)=rho^(g(b)) and P(I_tbj=1|I_(t-1)bj'=1)=(1-rho^(g(b)))/(n_i-1) for j!=j', where n_i is the number of pass rushers; each rho^(g) is estimated by maximum likelihood within EM as the expected fraction of retained assignments. primitives.name: Per-blocker rho_b ~ Beta empirical-Bayes: many snaps own transitions, few shrunk to position
primitives.verbatim_quote: A blocker seen on many snaps is governed by his own transitions, while one seen rarely is shrunk toward the position-level mean
assumptions: The transition probability varies by player (an elite tackle anchored on an edge rusher rarely switches, an interior lineman routinely passes off twists), so each blocker's rho_b varies by position with a common Beta prior rho_b~Beta(alpha^(g)_rho, beta^(g)_rho) within each position group; the hyperparameters are estimated by empirical Bayes so player-level estimates are partially pooled: a blocker seen on many snaps is governed by his own transitions, while one seen rarely is shrunk toward the position-level mean alpha/(alpha+beta). The Beta prior is printed math-font and reconstructed here.

layer2.mapping: The empirical-Bayes partial pooling is literally GSE's small-sample shrinkage for per-player assignment persistence.

primitives.name: Pre-snap multinomial-logistic prior over assignments (alignment/down/distance/formation)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Rather than initializing the hidden Markov chain with a uniform distribution over rushers, we encode this pre-snap belief with a multinomial-logistic model

symbol_and_unit_ledger.X0bj: pre-snap covariates for (blocker b, rusher j) pair (alignment, side, outermost, down/distance/formation interactions)

assumptions: Before the snap a blocker's responsibility is largely dictated by the protection scheme and defensive alignment (a left tackle is a-priori likely responsible for the edge rusher aligned to its side, modulated by down, distance, and formation); rather than initializing the hidden Markov chain uniformly over rushers, the pre-snap belief is encoded with a multinomial-logistic model P(I0bj=1)=exp{beta^(g(b))·X0bj}/sum_j' exp{beta^(g(b))·X0bj'}, with covariates for relative alignment, rusher lined-up alignment, and interactions with down/distance/formation, coefficients shared across plays but estimated per position group. The softmax prior is printed math-font and reconstructed here.

primitives.name: Disengaged (n_i+1)-th state: uniform emission, asymmetric shed/re-engage transitions
primitives.verbatim_quote: Because the disengaged state does not correspond to a rusher, it has a different emission distribution
assumptions: Because not every pass-blocker needs to be assigned a rusher, an (n_i+1)-th disengaged state is augmented to each blocker's latent state space; because the disengaged state does not correspond to a rusher it has a different emission distribution (uniform over position and orientation), assigned when no rusher's position-and-orientation density clears the background level; transitions to and from disengaged are asymmetric (block shed p_fail vs re-engage rho_null), reflecting that once a block is shed or lost it is difficult to re-engage.

layer2.mapping: The disengaged state with asymmetric shed/re-engage is literally GSE's block-failure-and-release latent state.
layer2.telemetry: (n_i+1)-th disengaged state; uniform position+orientation emission; assigned when no rusher density clears background c_bg; asymmetric p_fail (shed) vs rho_null (re-engage); shed block hard to re-engage

primitives.name: HMM params align with football intuition: OL/TE close to rusher, RB closer to QB
primitives.verbatim_quote: offensive linemen and tight ends position themselves close to the rusher they engage with
assumptions: Consistent with common protection designs, offensive linemen and tight ends position themselves close to the rusher they engage with (gamma_r approximately 0.82-0.89), whereas running backs position themselves closer to the quarterback (gamma_q approximately 0.45); positional variance is tightest for the interior line (approximately 1.0-1.4) and largest for backs, receivers, and fullbacks (approximately 4.6-5.9) who are not anchored to a fixed rusher; these estimates align closely with football intuition, supporting the model construction.

layer2.mapping: The position-resolved emission parameters are the same role-heterogeneity calibration GSE validates against football intuition.
layer2.telemetry: OL/TE gamma_r~0.82-0.89 (close to rusher); RB gamma_q~0.45 (closer to QB); sigma_D^2 interior ~1.0-1.4 tightest, RB/WR/FB ~4.6-5.9 largest; aligns football intuition

primitives.name: RB/WR low rho (~0.4): release into routes rather than sustain block
primitives.verbatim_quote: who are known to release into routes rather than sustaining a block over the course of the play
assumptions: The transition parameter rho is very high for linemen and tight ends (approximately 0.96-0.98), indicating these positions rarely switch, and far lower for running backs and wide receivers (approximately 0.4), who are known to release into routes rather than sustaining a block over the course of the play; the structured disengaged state separates that release from a genuine switch through the block-failure parameter p_fail (negligible for interior/TE approximately 0.01-0.02, large for backs/receivers approximately 0.55-0.58), and disengaged persistence rho_null approximately 0.97-1.00 is near-absorbing.

layer2.mapping: The release-vs-switch separation is literally GSE's distinction between route release and genuine block failure.
layer2.telemetry: rho OL/TE ~0.96-0.98 (rarely switch), RB/WR ~0.4 (release into routes); disengaged state separates release from switch via p_fail (interior/TE 0.01-0.02, backs/receivers 0.55-0.58); rho_null 0.97-1.00 near-absorbing

primitives.name: Attention n_eff(j,t)=sum_b theta(b,j,t): effective blockers a rusher faces, front-normalized
primitives.verbatim_quote: we normalize each rusher's attention within every play-frame relative to the average rusher on the field

symbol_and_unit_ledger.theta(b,j,t): assignment probability blocker b on rusher j at frame t
symbol_and_unit_ledger.n_eff(j,t): effective number of blockers facing rusher j at t
symbol_and_unit_ledger.front-normalized: divided by average over active rushers on the snap

assumptions: Attention is defined as the sum of the assignment probabilities assigned to a rusher at a given time-step, n_eff(j,t)=sum_b theta(b,j,t); aggregated over a play or season it is the number of effective blockers a rusher faces; because the number depends partly on the blocking scheme, each rusher's attention is normalized within every play-frame relative to the average rusher on the field so figures are comparable across three-, four-, and five-man fronts; top rushers generate about 1.5 times as many blockers per play as average. The attention sum is printed math-font and reconstructed here.
Attention effective-blocker sum printed math-font; reconstructed in labeled LaTeX and flagged.

primitives.name: Blocker entropy of marginal assignment distribution (normalized by log #rushers)
primitives.verbatim_quote: We quantify this with the entropy of a blocker's marginal assignment distribution over the rushers on a play
assumptions: A blocker who stays attached to a single rusher concentrates all assignment mass on one rusher, whereas one who passes off rushers, picks up stunts, or works combination blocks spreads mass across several; this is quantified with the entropy of a blocker's marginal assignment distribution over the rushers on a play, normalized by log of the number of rushers in the front so it is comparable across fronts of different sizes.

layer2.mapping: The front-normalized assignment entropy is literally GSE's switching-vs-anchored blocker dispersion metric.
layer2.telemetry: entropy of blocker marginal assignment distribution over rushers; normalized by log(#rushers) for cross-front comparability; concentrated (single rusher) vs spread (pass-off/stunt/combination)

primitives.name: Highest entropy = interior linemen (pass off twists/stunts); stickiest = tackles
primitives.verbatim_quote: The most variable (highest entropy) are predominantly interior linemen, consistent with their role in passing off twists, stunts, and looping rushers
assumptions: The stickiest blockers (lowest entropy) are almost exclusively offensive tackles, who tend to man up on a single edge rusher; the most variable (highest entropy) are predominantly interior linemen, consistent with their role in passing off twists, stunts, and looping rushers.

layer2.mapping: The entropy-by-position pattern is the same role-resolved switching signature GSE uses for OL archetype identification.
layer2.telemetry: stickiest (lowest entropy) = tackles (man single edge); most variable (highest entropy) = interior linemen (pass off twists/stunts/looping rushers)

primitives.name: Beaten = assigned rusher QB-side (d_rusher<d_blocker) AND STRAIN rising; won/release otherwise
primitives.verbatim_quote: In order to distinguish these different situations, we use geometric features together with STRAIN
assumptions: Three situations lead to a disengaged state: a blocker beaten (rusher crossed to the QB side), a blocker winning by driving the rusher away from the pocket, or a release with no other rusher to engage; to distinguish them, geometric features are used together with STRAIN: a disengaged blocker is beaten only when the assigned rusher (highest assignment probability) is on the quarterback side, d(rusher,QB)<d(blocker,QB), and that rusher's STRAIN is rising; won when the assigned rusher moves away with low or negative STRAIN; otherwise release.

layer2.mapping: The geometric-plus-STRAIN beaten/won/release classification is literally GSE's block-outcome disambiguation rule.
layer2.telemetry: 3 disengagement causes: beaten/won/release; beaten = assigned rusher QB-side d(rusher,QB)<d(blocker,QB) AND STRAIN rising; won = rusher moving away low/negative STRAIN; else release

primitives.name: Survival: snap-to-first-beaten, right-censored at throw; Kaplan-Meier RMST + beat rate
primitives.verbatim_quote: we take the time from the snap to the first time beaten by a rusher as a survival outcome, right-censored at the throw
primitives.latex: \mathrm{RMST}_b=\int_0^{\tau}\hat S_b(t)\,dt,\qquad \hat S_b\text{ Kaplan-Meier, right-censored at throw}

symbol_and_unit_ledger.S_b(t): blocker b survival function (probability block still held at t)
symbol_and_unit_ledger.right-censoring: at QB throw for blocks never beaten

assumptions: For each play and blocker, the time from the snap to the first time beaten by a rusher is taken as a survival outcome, right-censored at the throw for the majority of blocks never beaten, and summarized with the Kaplan-Meier restricted mean survival time RMST_b alongside the per-block beat rate BR_b; computing the same for a rusher gives RMST_j and shed rate BR_j, measuring how quickly and how often he beats the blocks he faces. The survival framing is described in prose; the Kaplan-Meier RMST is a standard estimator reconstructed here for completeness.
Kaplan-Meier RMST is a standard survival estimator; the paper describes it in prose, reconstructed in labeled LaTeX and flagged.

primitives.name: Opponent-adjusted discrete-time logistic survival: logit h = alpha + g1 t + g2 t^2 + beta_opp R + u_b

primitives.name: Continuous-time APM: Delta STRAIN ~ N(mu+R_j+Q_q - sum B_b theta + phi STRAIN); filtered posterior no lookahead

assumptions: The play-level plus-minus model is extended to continuous time by resolving it to the (play i, rusher j, frame t) level so that every rusher-frame is a distinct observation rather than a single play-level summary; the response is the one-frame change Delta STRAIN_ijt=STRAIN_i,j,t+1-STRAIN_ijt, modeled as Delta STRAIN_ijt ~ N(mu + R_j + Q_qi - sum_b B_b theta(b,j,t,i) + phi STRAIN_ijt, sigma^2); because the response looks one frame ahead, theta(b,j,t,i) is the filtered assignment posterior using tracking data only up to frame t (no lookahead); equivalently a first-order autoregression of next-frame STRAIN with coefficient 1+phi, mean-reversion phi-hat=-0.059, fit by NUTS on 1.1M rusher-frames. reasoning_traces.think: The retrocausal genealogy of this paper is the tracking-data turn in offensive-line evaluation. Abhijit Brahme, Ishan Mehta, Gregory Matthews, and Alexander Franks, posting to arXiv in September 2026 as 2609.33664, start from the premise that statistical analysis of offensive linemen has been hindered by the lack of easily measurable quantities, since linemen are noticed only when they err on rare events like sacks and missed blocks whose counts are unreliable estimates of ability. The work adapts the defensive-matchup hidden Markov model that Franks and colleagues built for basketball in 2015 to football pass protection, and it sits in the lineage of Alamar and Weinstein-Gould's block-hold-time studies, Macdonald's adjusted plus-minus, Burke's pass block win rate, Nguyen's STRAIN pressure metric, and Fernandez and Bornn's soccer space-control surfaces, while drawing on the Kalman filter for smoothing and the von Mises distribution for circular orientation. The recursive theory of mind is the latent-assignment HMM and its emission geometry. The latent state is the identity of the rusher a blocker is engaged with, evolving frame by frame as linemen pass off rushers or stunt; the core assumption is that a blocker positions between their assigned rusher and the quarterback, so the positional emission is a bivariate normal centered on a weighted point of the rusher-to-quarterback segment, and the orientation emission is a von Mises distribution centered opposite the rusher because blockers face and stay square to their assignment. The transition probability encodes stickiness, with a per-blocker Beta prior partially pooled by position so that data-rich blockers govern their own switches and data-poor ones shrink to the position mean; a pre-snap multinomial-logistic prior encodes protection-scheme responsibility from alignment, down, distance, and formation; and an augmented disengaged state with asymmetric shed and re-engage transitions separates a beaten block from a route release. Cross-layer veto adjudication is the suite of metrics derived from the assignment posterior and their external validation. Attention sums assignment probabilities into an effective-blocker count front-normalized for cross-scheme comparability, blocker entropy measures switching versus anchoring, the geometric-plus-STRAIN rule disambiguates beaten from won from release, and a right-censored Kaplan-Meier survival yields restricted-mean hold time and beat rates, upgraded to an opponent-adjusted discrete-time logistic frailty that moves Trent Williams from fifteenth to third among tackles. The continuous-time plus-minus regresses the one-frame change in STRAIN on assignment-weighted blocker effects using the filtered posterior to avoid lookahead, with player effects shrunk toward position-height-weight archetypes; pocket control and value-weighted near-quarterback space then credit rushers both for personal pressure and for the space they generate by pulling blockers off teammates. The implementation invariants map directly onto GSE. The matchup HMM is GSE's offensive-line causal-breakdown assignment kernel; STRAIN is GSE's distance-normalized closing-rate pressure measure; the assignment-weighted continuous plus-minus is GSE's partial-credit pressure-prevention attribution replacing all-or-nothing stints; the censored survival and opponent-adjusted frailty are GSE's quality-of-competition-corrected block-sustain rating; the pocket-control logistic surface and distance-decayed space quality are GSE's pass-protection space-ownership kernel; and the directed assignment-flow space generation is GSE's teammate-freeing credit for double-team-drawing interior rushers. The filtered-posterior no-lookahead discipline and the empirical-Bayes partial pooling are GSE's leakage-free temporal and small-sample shrinkage requirements. The validation results make the credibility concrete and honest. Derived purely from tracking geometry and STRAIN without hand labels, the assignments recover independently charted PFF responsibilities, placing a mean of 0.77 of engaged probability mass on the charted rusher and agreeing on the most-assigned rusher 87.5 percent of the time across 44,037 blocker-plays; the rush-side metrics validate strongly, with the continuous-time rusher effect correlating 0.57 with PFF pressure rate and 0.46 with sack rate, while the block-side metrics validate directionally, the blocker effect correlating 0.32 with pressures allowed. The recovered parameters align with football intuition: linemen and tight ends anchor close to their rusher with high stickiness, running backs and receivers release into routes with low stickiness and high failure hazard, and the leading space generators are interior linemen who command double teams and free teammates, ranking high in attention but low in personal pressure. The caveats close the account with the scope limits that bound the claim. The model relies primarily on positioning and does not fully separate a blocker actively impeding a rusher from one merely in the right place, a missed block while nominally assigned, so a two-layer HMM could additionally infer engagement status; blocker evaluation remains an associational estimate rather than a causal one, and a causal reformulation is flagged as the harder open problem for actionable coaching insight; and the probabilistic instrument is agnostic to the outcome, so any frame-level pressure measure could replace STRAIN without changing the evaluation machinery. The invariant for GSE is to adopt the matchup-HMM assignment kernel, the STRAIN pressure measure, the assignment-weighted continuous plus-minus with filtered no-lookahead posteriors, the censored opponent-adjusted survival, the pocket-control and value-weighted space surfaces, and the directed space-generation credit, while carrying the impeding-versus-positioned limitation, the associational-not-causal caveat, and the outcome-agnostic flexibility as honest bounds on what the tracking-derived blocking model can claim. The two-dimensional pass-rush value plot reinforces the hidden-value point: front-normalized attention and the continuous-time rusher effect are strongly negatively related at Pearson minus zero point seven eight, so edge rushers like T.J. Watt face fewer blockers and build STRAIN quickly while interior linemen draw more blockers but build pressure slowly, and the rare rushers who draw extra attention and still build STRAIN quickly, such as Cameron Heyward, mark the genuinely disruptive exceptions that a personal-pressure-only metric would undervalue.

universal_lens: A hidden-Markov treatment of NFL pass protection infers frame-by-frame probabilistic blocker-to-rusher assignments from tracking geometry — a blocker positioned between rusher and quarterback and facing opposite the rusher, with sticky transitions, a pre-snap scheme prior, and a disengaged state — and turns the assignment posterior into rusher attention, blocker switching entropy, censored block-shedding survival with opponent adjustment, assignment-weighted continuous-time plus-minus on STRAIN, pocket space control, and directed teammate-freeing space generation; validated against independent PFF charting (0.77 engaged mass, 87.5% agreement, rush-side correlations 0.57/0.46), it recovers elite rushers and protectors and exposes the hidden value of double-team-drawing interior linemen, while remaining associational rather than causal and unable to fully separate active impedance from mere positioning.
